settings-analysis.body: C menu add grid_view merge travel_explore code description fact_check content_paste_go database cloud_upload article group lan webhook credit_card cable settings help chat workspace_premium CA Analysis Settings Targets & Execution per repo Where approved changes land, and where they run. Base branch filter Only PRs targeting these branches are analyzed. Separate with commas, e.g. main, release/*. Use * for every branch. Max files per analysis Cost/latency guard. Beyond this the run is marked partial. Path scope One glob per line. Monorepo subtree scoping — e.g. apps/web/**. When should we run your tests? Impact analysis tells you which cases a change affects. This decides whether we also run them. Don't run them Analyse and report only. Nothing is executed. After the pull request merges Run the affected cases against your chosen environment once the merged build is deployed. Before it merges Run against the pull request's own build, so the PR carries real pass/fail before anyone approves it. Environment * Production Staging The run uses this environment's variables, overriding what each case would otherwise use. warning Cases with a fixed URL will not test the new build. The environment above reaches steps that use environment variables. A step with a hard-coded URL, a global, or a URL written into an AI-agent instruction keeps pointing where it already pointed — so it will pass without having tested this deployment. Promotion, Governance & Operations Guardrails for applying changes and reporting back to the PR. Post PR comment Off leaves only the check. Post status check A check run on GitHub, a commit status on GitLab. Advisory either way — it never fails the build. Suppress paths One glob per line. Never analyse generated or vendored code — the biggest source of noise. Every value here is snapshotted onto the analysis row at analysis time — the “Decided under” line in each row's detail renders that snapshot, not live config. save Update

settings-bug-repro.body: C menu add grid_view merge travel_explore code description fact_check content_paste_go database cloud_upload article group lan webhook credit_card cable settings help chat workspace_premium CA Bug Reproduction Settings Reproduce a bug from a plain-text report — a ticket, a Slack message, anything. The AI parses the report; these settings decide which Environment and Data Profile it reproduces with, and what to fall back to when neither is specified. Defaults Used when a report doesn't name a specific Environment or Data Profile. Both are managed under Environments and Data Profiles — this only picks which one Bug Reproduction reaches for by default. Environment Select an Environment Production Staging The environment reproduction runs against unless the report names one. Data Profile No data profiles for this environment Test-data profile attached to the default environment above. Recognized label formats Add either of these to a ticket to pick the exact Environment or Data Profile to reproduce with, instead of the defaults above — the AI matches the value after the colon by name. Environment Data Profile env:value environment:value dataprofile:value When to reproduce Choose which tickets start a reproduction automatically, and which actions trigger one. Applies to Linear, Jira and ClickUp; for ClickUp tasks, trigger labels are task tags. Only tickets with a trigger label Recommended. Nothing runs unless a ticket carries one of the labels below. Every new ticket Labels are ignored. Every new ticket is reproduced — set a daily cap below. Trigger labels Only tickets with one of these labels are reproduced. ClickUp tasks match them as tags. info Connect Linear to choose from your workspace's labels. You can still type a label name. Try again Trigger on A new ticket is created Reproduce as soon as a matching ticket appears. A trigger label is added Reproduce when someone labels an existing ticket. The title or description is edited Re-runs when the reporter supplies more detail. Each re-run is a full reproduction. Someone comments /reproduce Always available to a person asking explicitly, label or not. Limits Max reproductions per ticket Max reproductions per day Leave blank for no limit. Each reproduction runs a full browser session, so a broad trigger on a busy project adds up quickly. Re-validate fixes When a reproduced ticket moves to one of these statuses, re-run its saved test and comment Fixed, Not fixed or Could not verify. Each re-validation is charged as a test run. Only tickets ContextQA reproduced earlier are re-run. save Update
